summary: This project is built to provide an opportunity to understand the basics of space exploration for beginners. It is a simulation of working inside space outposts on the Moon, Mars, and Titan using real NASA telemetry data. In addition, I added dynamic environmental hazards and resource trade-offs to make this simulation engaging and fun for everyone.
details: GUSSX Astro-Game is an interactive 2D browser-based habitat survival trainer designed for students (ages 7–12) to learn how astronauts manage closed-loop life support systems on the Moon, Mars, and Titan. Inside a two-story planetary dome, the player must survive a 5-minute shift by balancing limited Power, Oxygen, Radiation/Thermal Shields, Hunger, and Stamina. Every action involves a strategic trade-off: recharging life support consumes energy and time, growing crops (Space Sprouts, Lunar Potatoes, Martian Soybeans) requires planning around sprint exhaustion and hunger, and planetary hazards (solar flares, dust storms, cryo-methane squalls) force rapid shield management. Built from scratch using vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript Canvas API, calibrated with real planetary telemetry from NASA.
